correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 and all prescribed positive radii and parameters c>||w||r_m, rotation gives exact \dot s=2F(s)(epsilon xi+beta eta). The factorization proves circle invariance, the exact cosine integral gives the original-time period and Floquet exponent, and the strict negative geometric bracket gives alternating hyperbolicity for epsilon!=0. For epsilon=0, the exact H integral and analytic desingularization J_i, with nonzero normal derivative, give two-sided period annuli. Polynomial divisibility proves optimal degree n>=2m. Companion checker verifies symbolic identities, 27 quadratures, 2 monodromy examples and 4 local neutral returns, but finite checks are not universal proofs.

originality.rationale: Source arXiv:2610.33226v1 supplies the general circle normal form and a one-circle quadratic inner-product criterion; these are acknowledged as prior. The new joint claim concerns every integer m≥2 at degree 2m, an explicitly integrable codimension-one simultaneous neutral wall, and exact common-parameter periods/Floquet multipliers. The full 2015 realization paper allows prescribing period/stability configurations but its distinct, generally higher-degree construction does not imply this particular family or neutral analytic annuli. Inspected related published research claims use different equations. An inaccessible detailed 2016 circular-cycle paper and possible implicit general methods remain priority risks, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Complete 2016 circular-cycle classification was inaccessible in bounded open-access searches; a general result there could contain a stronger covering family.
Other general integrability/limit-cycle constructions might implicitly imply some formulas without stating the simultaneous orthogonality wall.
No independent scientific audit; the novel joint theorem is not an assertion of absolute publication priority.

value.rationale: At the classically optimal degree 2m, a natural smallest nonconstant affine angular factor yields a codimension-one parameter wall that simultaneously exchanges any finite collection of alternating hyperbolic concentric limit cycles for analytic period annuli. Exact shared-parameter physically timed periods and Floquet logs distinguish it from known mere existence or circle-count bounds, and m may be arbitrarily large. The structural bifurcation and integrability mechanism are mathematically motivated and can guide classification of higher-degree angular perturbations. Scope is intentionally this explicit family, not all planar fields.
